# Environment annotations — every (name, verb) pair snug has something to say
# about, and the exact text it says. Regenerate with:
#   go test ./internal/policy -update
#
# NONE OF THESE IS A REFUSAL. Every pair below is ACCEPTED — a profile's author
# is a human on the trusted side of snug's boundary, and snug has only
# allowlists. What the table buys is that the row says what the tool will DO,
# on --dry-run and on `snug profile show`. A name missing from this file hands
# over its value with nothing said about it.
#
# Only pairs a profile can actually WRITE are listed: a verb the variable's
# TYPE refuses (environ.merge on a scalar, environ.sanitise on MANPATH) can
# never reach a screen, and a type refusal is snug declining an operation
# rather than denying anyone anything. See internal/policy/testdata/
# refusals.txt for those.

## exact names

ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL       set       ← every request the agent makes, conversation included, goes to this endpoint instead of Anthropic's
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL       inherit   ← every request the agent makes, conversation included, goes to this endpoint instead of Anthropic's
BASH_ENV                 set       ← every non-interactive bash SOURCES this file at startup; grant the path in the same profile
BASH_ENV                 inherit   ← every non-interactive bash SOURCES this file at startup, and the file is chosen on the host, outside any profile
CARGO_HOME               inherit   ← taking the host's value points cargo back at the host's config, which is the file "generate, don't bind" exists to avoid; `set` it to a path a profile authored

CC                       inherit   ← make's implicit rules run this as the compiler (measured)
DOCKER_CONFIG            inherit   ← taking the host's value points docker back at the host's config, credentials included; `set` it to a path a profile authored
